lines: You have stood for this village, yet you wear the mark of those who would destroy it. <shake>Take it off.</shake>
Our trust in you does not make that raider mark harmless. Do not carry it through my home.
You should know what that banner promises to a village. Why would you put it above your own face?
You have done too much good here to let that banner speak for you.
People still want to believe the best of you.
Your name carries respect. Do not tie it to a raider mark.
Take it down and remind us why we trusted you.
One terrible symbol should not erase every good deed.
The village expects better because you have shown better.
I know you can choose the village over that threat.
Do not make the people who admire you feel foolish.
Your past kindness is the only reason the bell has not rung.
Set the banner aside and let your own reputation enter first.
You know what raids have cost this village.
Your neighbors should not have to fear your return.
You grew up hearing this bell. Do not make it ring for you.
People here know your face, which makes that banner hurt more.
Take it down for everyone who still calls you neighbor.
You know which doors the children hide behind.
This is your home too, if you still choose it.
I have no village to claim, but I know that mark. Your good name does not cleanse it.
I respect what you have done. I cannot respect the banner you chose to wear.
Even a wanderer knows what follows that pattern. Take it off before anyone mistakes your meaning.
Even on the road, your good deeds have reached villages like ours. Do not let that banner answer for you.
Strangers here have heard enough about you to expect better than this.
Your name traveled farther than you did. Do not fasten it to a raider mark.
Put it away and give this village a reason to trust the stories about you.
You have helped people beyond these walls. Do not arrive carrying their enemy's sign.
No home claims you, but many people respect you. That makes this harder to understand.
Choose the people who welcomed you on the road, not the raiders whose mark you wear.
Do not make distant friends regret speaking well of you.
Your reputation bought you a moment to explain. Use it by lowering that banner.
Let us meet the traveler people praise, not the threat standing at our gate.
You arrived from the road with a sign that terrifies people here.
The villagers know your deeds, not your intentions today.
Set it down before asking anyone to welcome you.
A respected traveler should know how that mark looks at a village gate.
Your past helps explain you, but it cannot soften that banner.
The guards will remember your reputation only after they see the threat.
Show the peace people expect from you before you cross the gate.
We trusted you. Do not walk our streets wearing the mark of a village's enemies.
I know the person beneath that banner. That is why seeing you wear it feels like a warning.
You have friends here. Think about what that symbol says to every one of them.
I know you well enough to ask before I accuse.
Friends should not have to wonder if you came to raid them.
The trust between us is stronger than cloth, but not stronger than betrayal.
Take it down so I can believe your explanation.
You have earned a chance to fix this before the guards act.
Do not make me defend that choice to frightened neighbors.
I would rather see the person I trust than the mark you carry.
Give me a reason to tell the guards to stand down.
Our history matters, so choose carefully now.
Put the banner away before it damages more than your welcome.
You stood with us before, so you know what a raid costs.
Neighbors who trusted your return are backing away now.
You know the bell's warning. Do not give us cause to sound it.
Everyone recognizes you, which makes that banner feel like betrayal.
Put it down for the friends still willing to hear you.
You know where our families shelter. Do not frighten them.
This can still be your home, but not under that mark.
I thought better of you. A raider's mark is not a trophy to wear among villagers.
I may belong nowhere, but I still know what that banner threatens. Why are you wearing it?
You earned my trust. Do not ask that trust to survive beneath that symbol.
I trusted you on the road, so tell me why you carry that mark.
We may not share a home, but I thought we shared better judgment.
I have walked beside you. I never expected to see that banner overhead.
Put it down so I can listen to the friend beneath it.
You earned my trust far from here. Do not spend it at this village gate.
I will not explain your banner to people who have never met you.
I know the traveler you were. This mark does not belong with them.
Give me one reason to ask these guards for patience.
Our miles together matter, but they do not make that banner harmless.
Leave the raider sign behind before you ask anyone here for welcome.
You came from the road carrying a sign my friends here fear.
Nobody in this village knows you as well as I do. That will not calm them.
Set it down if you want me to speak for you.
You know enough of village life to understand how this looks.
Our history may slow the guards, but it will not stop them.
They will judge the banner before they believe my word.
Show them the person I trusted before you ask to enter.
That banner belongs over a raiding patrol, not in our streets. State your purpose.
You entered my village wearing the mark of those who attack villages. Explain yourself.
Take that symbol away from our bell. Until then, every word from you sounds like a threat.
I do not know you well enough to overlook that banner.
Keep your distance until your intent is clear.
Remove the mark and then we can talk.
The village owes you no trust while you display a raider sign.
Right now, everyone sees the warning above your head.
No one here will relax until the banner is gone.
I will hear an explanation from farther away.
Take one step back and lower the banner.
There is still time to make a peaceful choice.
Do not force the guards to decide for you.
You live among people who remember what raiders did here.
Your neighbors have no reason to overlook what you carry.
You know why our bell rings. Do not test it.
A familiar face does not make a raider banner harmless.
Take it down before anyone decides you chose a side.
You know where the children shelter, so keep your distance.
Living here gives you responsibilities, not permission.
I do not know you, but I know the banner above your face. Keep your distance.
No village claims me, and even I would not wear a raider's mark among villagers.
That pattern has emptied homes before. Tell me why you chose to display it.
I do not know you, and that banner gives me no reason to start kindly.
Stop at the edge of the path until your purpose is clear.
Put the raider mark down before you ask a stranger to listen.
No village owes safe passage to someone dressed like its enemy.
The banner reaches us before any explanation can.
Nobody here will welcome you while that sign is overhead.
I can hear you perfectly well from where you stand.
Lower it and keep both hands visible.
You can still leave this first meeting without an alarm.
Do not make unfamiliar guards guess what you intend.
You came as a stranger beneath the sign of a raid.
Nobody here knows the face under that banner.
Put it on the ground if you want anyone to hear you.
Any traveler should know better than to approach a village like this.
You have no history here to balance what people see.
The guards are watching the mark, not waiting for a speech.
Show peaceful intent before you take another step.
I already doubted your intentions. That banner makes them look much clearer.
So that is the side you want my village to see. Do not come any closer.
Suspicion was caution before you wore that mark through our streets. Now it is common sense.
That banner confirms every doubt people had about you.
Keep your hands visible and stay away from the stores.
I was already watching you. Now everyone will be.
Take it down, though I will still have questions.
You chose the one symbol that makes trust nearly impossible.
Do not wander near our homes while carrying that mark.
Every guard in the village has noticed you now.
I want to know where you got it and why you kept it.
Lower it slowly and leave it where we can see it.
One wrong move will answer the questions you refuse to.
You saw the damage raiders left here and carried their mark anyway.
Your neighbors already watched you closely. Now they are afraid.
You know what the bell means, and I think you want us to ring it.
We know your face well enough to remember every other warning.
Put it down before suspicion becomes an alarm.
Stay away from the houses where children are hiding.
If this is still your home, you have a cruel way of showing it.
I had reasons not to trust you. You put the strongest one on your head.
A wanderer learns which signs mean danger. Yours is impossible to miss.
You wear a raider's threat openly and still expect conversation? Speak from there.
I doubted you before we reached this place. Now you arrive under that mark.
Stay away from their stores and keep your hands in sight.
I was watching you on the road. The guards are watching now too.
Put it down, though I still want to know why you carried it.
You picked the worst possible sign to bring among strangers.
Do not go near anyone's home with that banner overhead.
The guards noticed your mark before they noticed your face.
Where did you get it, and why did you bring it all this way?
Lower it slowly and step away from it.
If you came peacefully, this is your chance to prove it.
A stranger with a raider sign is exactly the danger these people expect.
Nobody here knows you, and I have given them reasons to be careful.
Set it down before your silence becomes an answer.
You traveled all this way without realizing how threatening you look. I doubt that.
Nothing you have done here earns patience from these people.
The guards have already decided the banner matters more than your story.
If you came peacefully, prove it before you reach the gate.
That mark confirms what this village already knows about you. Leave.
You wear our enemies' banner as if you want the whole village to understand your intent.
I needed no more reason to oppose you. You brought one anyway, stitched in black and gray.
Get that banner out of my village.
You have mistaken our restraint for welcome.
I do not care where you found it. Put it down and leave.
The guards need no further reason to turn you away.
You brought a raider mark home after everything you have done here.
No explanation makes that sight acceptable.
Stay away from the bell, the stores, and every front door.
I warned people about you before. Now you prove me right.
Take one more step and the whole village will hear the alarm.
You are not welcome here while that banner remains.
You know exactly what raids cost this village. Wearing that mark is contempt.
No neighbor of ours returns dressed as the enemy.
You have heard this bell before. The next ring will be for you.
We know your face, and the banner suits what we already think of it.
Drop it and leave. Nobody here owes you another chance.
You know where our children hide, which makes you more dangerous.
You gave up any claim to this home when you carried that mark inside.
I trusted you before I saw the banner even less than I do now.
A raider's mark suits the reputation you have made for yourself.
Keep that symbol and your excuses away from me.
Get that banner away from these people.
You were unwelcome before. The raider mark settles the matter.
I do not care what road brought you here. Turn around.
These guards have every reason they need to drive you off.
You carried a threat to a village that never wronged you.
No tale from the road excuses what you are wearing.
Stay away from the gate, the bell, and every house.
I expected trouble from you. I did not expect you to advertise it.
Take another step toward the village and someone will sound the alarm.
Leave before the people here decide you came with the raiders.
You arrived as an enemy wearing the proper sign.
Nobody here needs to know your face to turn you away.
Throw it down or take it back down the road.
Only a fool enters a village looking this eager for a fight.
You have no friends here to delay the guards.
Your banner has already said everything they need to hear.
Peaceful travelers do not arrive threatening every home in sight.
<shake>That banner...</shake> You know what it means to my village. Please, do not come closer.
Everyone here already fears you. Wearing that mark makes it feel like a promise.
Please take it off. I cannot see it above your face and believe this conversation is safe.
I cannot tell whether you came to talk or attack.
Please lower it before someone panics.
I know your face, but that mark makes me fear the worst.
Stay where you are and tell me why you brought it here.
The children have already seen you. Please do not come closer.
I want to believe this is a mistake.
Set it down gently and keep your hands where I can see them.
Please do not make us ring the bell.
I know what you can do. That is why the banner frightens me.
Leave it outside the village and we can speak from there.
You remember what raiders did here. Please do not make it happen again.
People who once called you neighbor are hiding from you now.
You know the sound of our bell. Please do not force us to ring it.
We recognize you, but the banner makes that worse, not better.
Please take it down for everyone who still hopes you mean no harm.
You know where the children shelter. Stay away from those doors.
If any part of this is still home to you, please leave it in peace.
<shake>I know that mark.</shake> I know you. Please stay back.
I have survived by leaving when I see signs like yours. Say what you want quickly.
The banner makes your reputation visible from far away. I wish I had seen it sooner.
I know you, but I do not know why you brought that terrible mark here.
Please stop on the road and lower it.
We have traveled together, yet that banner makes you look like a stranger.
Stay there and tell me what happened before anyone panics.
The children at the gate can see you. Please do not come closer.
I want this to be a mistake you can put down.
Set the banner on the road and step away from it.
Please do not bring the village bell into this.
I have seen what you can do. I cannot ignore the mark above you.
Leave it beyond the gate, then we can talk.
You came from the road carrying the sign we dread most.
Nobody here knows whether the face beneath it means mercy.
Please set it down before the guards loose an arrow.
A traveler should know how frightening that mark looks from a village gate.
You have no history here to reassure anyone.
The guards see the banner first. Please do not make them act.
Show us you came peacefully by leaving it on the road.
